query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The nitriding treatment of Ti-6Al-4V alloy will increase its surface hardness and wear resistance due to the formation of a hard TiN layer.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 500-600°C, Time: 10-20 hours, Atmosphere: Nitrogen-rich environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a hard TiN layer on the surface
generation.mechanism: Diffusion of nitrogen into the titanium alloy, forming a hard and wear-resistant TiN layer
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased surface hardness and wear resistance due to the formation of a hard TiN layer
generation.boundary: The nitriding treatment is expected to be effective under the specified conditions, but may not be suitable for all applications or environments.
generation.uncertainty: The main risk is the potential for incomplete or non-uniform nitriding, which could lead to inconsistent surface properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the surface hardness and wear resistance of nitrided and untreated Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided samples do not show a significant increase in surface hardness and wear resistance compared to the untreated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The third way is to modify its surface structure through surface engineering technology [], such as carburizing, nitriding and boronizing. For example, with Ni45(CoCrFe)40(AlTi)15 surface nitriding [], AlN, CrN and TiN phases are formed on the surface, effectively increasing the surface hardness of the alloy from 8.8 GPa to 14.9 GPa. Furthermore, the utilization of shot peening, laser remelting and various other technologies also have the potential to enhance the surface characteristics of HEAs [,]. Al, Ti and Cr are widely used in alloys because of their effects on microstructure, strengthening and oxidation resistance. V is commonly used to improve friction and wear properties because its atomic size deforms the crystal structure of BCC and FCC alloys. As a lightweight alloy, the mechanical properties and corrosion resistance of the HEA of AlCrVTi have been studied, but the effect of the content of Nb on the wear resistance of the HEA has not been studied [,,,]. In this paper, AlCrTiVNbx (x = 0.3, 0.4, 0.5) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc melting and annealed at 1000 °C for 2 h to investigate the changes in microstructure and mechanical properties before and after annealing. The potentiodynamic tests and associated results suggest that the titanium free HEAs are performing better than titanium-based alloys. The EIS test results follow a similar pattern, and it was noted that AlCoCr1.3FeNi1.3 is the best performing alloy for both cases (the logarithm of the corrosion current was ~−5.2 (A/cm2)). We have compared the available data for pure titanium metal where electrochemical corrosion tests were conducted under a NaCl deposit in wet oxygen at 600 °C []. In that case the logarithm of corrosion current value was ~−4.35 (A/cm2) []. In the case of Ti-6Al-4V alloy the log (corrosion current) value in ~1% NaCl was ~−5.75 (A/cm2) []. In case of γ Ti-Al alloy the corrosion current value was ~0.16 (μA/cm2). In the case of accelerated corrosion-based mass loss tests (see Figure A13), the highest loss was noted for alloy 4, namely AlCo0.9CrFeNiMn0.9. Whereas, the lowest loss was noted for alloy 2 (CoCr1.3FeMnNi0.7). This is moreover consistent with potentiodynamic scan test results and associated corrosion currents.
